how: Each feed page was read in the desktop app's built-in browser with tools/humanization/pangram_feed_read.js in compact mode: the result's fields, the SHA-256 of its checked text, and its windows as compact lines (WINDOWS-A.txt, WINDOWS-B.txt, each checked here against the page's own SHA-256 of that line). The checked text is rebuilt from the pasted payload (tools/humanization/substack_check_text.py); B's matches the page's SHA-256 as it is, and A's once the one no-break space of his "Breadcrumbing is" is a plain space, as Substack shows it (the preview check of turn 119 found the same).

ai_windows.text: The peer doesn’t become your permanent parent, though. They show you a capacity, help you get the hang of it, and give it back to you, which is borrowed adulthood in its healthiest form.
